 UPSC Civil Services Mains Result 2026 Declared, 2,526 Candidates Qualify for Interview 
 Successful candidates advance to the personality test stage, with the commission providing a window from November 11 to 25 for updating relevant application details.
 Latest News Art and Culture 
 By Bold News Digital 
 On Nov 9, 2026 
 Share 
 NEW DELHI, Nov 9: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) has shortlisted 2,526 candidates for the Personality Test after declaring the results of the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026, marking the beginning of the final stage of the country’s prestigious civil services selection process.
 Candidates who cleared the written examination will now compete for appointments to the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), Indian Police Service (IPS) and other Group A and Group B Central Services.
 According to the commission’s notification, the Mains examination was conducted between August 21 and August 30, 2026. A total of 13,343 candidates had appeared for the written stage after qualifying through the Civil Services Preliminary Examination. Of these, 2,526 have secured a place in the list of candidates eligible to proceed to the interview round.
Press Information Bureau+1
The written examination result was published on November 5 and is available on the commission’s official website. Candidates can access the result through the written results section by opening the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 document and checking their roll numbers.
 The Personality Test represents the concluding stage of the Civil Services Examination and is designed to evaluate candidates beyond their academic knowledge and written performance. It assesses their personality, intellectual abilities, decision-making skills, communication, leadership qualities and suitability for administrative responsibilities.
 The commission has instructed all shortlisted candidates to complete or update their Detailed Application Form (DAF) through its online portal. The submission facility will remain available from November 11 to November 25, 2026, until 6 pm.
 Candidates must provide accurate information regarding their educational qualifications, employment history, personal particulars and other details required for the selection process. Those who have already submitted certain information during earlier stages must also log in, verify the existing details and complete the final submission as instructed.
 The commission has made it clear that failure to submit the required information within the stipulated period could result in the non-issuance of the e-Summon Letter for the interview.
 Applicants are therefore advised to carefully review their application details before completing the process. Any discrepancies in personal information, academic qualifications or eligibility documents should be addressed within the prescribed timeline.
 The UPSC has also asked shortlisted candidates to keep their original certificates ready for verification during the Personality Test. These include documents relating to age, educational qualifications, community status, Economically Weaker Section (EWS) eligibility and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), wherever applicable.
 Candidates claiming reservation benefits under Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, EWS and other eligible categories must produce valid supporting certificates. Applicants seeking applicable exemptions or relaxations will also have to provide the necessary documentation.
 The commission has clarified that the candidature of those shortlisted remains provisional until their eligibility is verified in accordance with the examination rules. Qualification in the written examination does not automatically guarantee final selection or appointment.
 The interview schedule has not yet been announced. The commission will communicate the dates and other relevant instructions separately through its official website.
 The Personality Tests will be conducted at the UPSC office located at Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi. Candidates will be required to download their e-Summon Letters through the commission’s website or the designated online application portal. No physical summons letters will be dispatched.
 The interview stage carries considerable importance because it provides the commission an opportunity to assess candidates’ overall suitability for public service. While the written examination tests their understanding of various subjects, the personality assessment focuses on their ability to apply knowledge, respond to challenging situations and demonstrate sound judgement.
 Candidates are generally expected to remain informed about national and international developments, governance issues, public administration, social challenges and matters connected with their educational and professional backgrounds.
 The interview panel may also examine their understanding of the subjects they studied, their hobbies, professional experiences and the information provided in their application forms.
 For many aspirants, reaching the interview stage represents the culmination of years of preparation and sustained effort. The Civil Services Examination is among India’s most competitive recruitment processes, attracting graduates from diverse academic disciplines and professional backgrounds.
 The selection procedure consists of three major stages: the Preliminary Examination, the Main Examination and the Personality Test. Candidates must qualify at each stage to remain eligible for further consideration.
 The Preliminary Examination serves as the screening stage, while the Mains assesses candidates through written papers covering a wide range of subjects. Those who clear the written stage are invited for the final personality assessment.
 The final merit list is prepared on the basis of performance in the Main Examination and Personality Test, subject to applicable eligibility requirements and reservation provisions.
 The number of candidates shortlisted for interviews is determined through the commission’s established selection process. Their eventual allocation to different services will depend on their final merit position, preferences, category and the availability of vacancies.
 UPSC has advised applicants to regularly monitor its official website for announcements concerning interview dates, e-Summon Letters and other formalities.
 Candidates should also ensure that the information provided in their online forms matches their supporting documents, as discrepancies may create difficulties during verification.
 The commission will release the marksheets of candidates after completion of the Personality Tests and declaration of the final result, in accordance with its examination procedures.
 With 2,526 candidates advancing to the final stage, attention has now shifted towards interview preparations and the completion of mandatory documentation. The upcoming assessment will determine which candidates move closer to securing positions in India’s premier administrative and allied services.
